def: Treating a person or group worse than others because of who they are, for example their sex, age or origin.

formal.ex: The Company will not tolerate any form of [[unlawful discrimination]] in recruitment, pay or promotion.

everyday.ex: She's convinced it was [[discrimination]], pure and simple.

collocations: discrimination on the grounds of age
note_fr: Attention aux prépositions : « discrimination AGAINST women », « on the grounds of sex » (UK) ou « on the basis of sex » (US). Jamais « discrimination towards » ni « discrimination about ».

def: To treat someone less well than others for a reason the law does not allow.

formal.ex: An employer must not [[discriminate against]] a job applicant because of his or her age.

everyday.ex: He feels he's been [[treated unfairly]] ever since he mentioned his health condition.

collocations: to discriminate against someone because of their age
to discriminate on the basis of sex
note_fr: Le verbe anglais est intransitif : on ne dit pas « to discriminate someone » mais « to discriminate AGAINST someone ». Au passif : « she was discriminated against ».

def: One of the personal characteristics, such as sex, age or religion, that the law forbids an employer to take into account.

formal.ex: Trade union activity is a [[prohibited ground of discrimination]] under the French Labour Code.
formal.ex_us: Union activity is a [[prohibited basis of discrimination]] under the French Labor Code.

everyday.ex: You can't turn someone down [[on the grounds of]] their accent.
everyday.ex_us: You can't turn someone down [[on the basis of]] their accent.

collocations: a ground covered by the law
note_fr: Le Code du travail français énumère plus d'une vingtaine de critères, bien plus que le droit britannique (neuf « protected characteristics ») ou le droit fédéral américain. « Motive » désigne le mobile d'une personne, pas le critère légal.

def: Less favourable treatment because of a person's race, colour, nationality or ethnic or national origin.

formal.uk: discrimination on the grounds of race or ethnic origin
formal.us: discrimination on the basis of race or national origin
formal.ex: The policy prohibits [[discrimination on the grounds of race or ethnic origin]].
formal.ex_us: The policy prohibits [[discrimination on the basis of race or national origin]].

everyday.ex: He's bringing a [[race discrimination]] claim against his former employer.

note_fr: En anglais juridique, « race » est un terme courant et neutre (« race discrimination », « race relations »), alors que le droit français parle plutôt d'origine ou d'appartenance vraie ou supposée à une ethnie. Ne traduisez pas « origine » par « origin » tout seul : précisez « ethnic » ou « national ».

def: Treating someone less well because they are considered too old or too young.

formal.uk: discrimination on the grounds of age
formal.us: discrimination on the basis of age
formal.ex: Selecting employees for training by reference to their date of birth may constitute [[discrimination on the grounds of age]].
formal.ex_us: Selecting employees for training by reference to their date of birth may constitute [[discrimination on the basis of age]].

everyday.ex: Asking for a 'digital native' in a job advert is asking for an [[age discrimination]] claim.

informal.ex: There's a fair bit of [[ageism]] in that team, if I'm honest.

collocations: to be passed over because of one's age
note_fr: Aux États-Unis, la loi fédérale ne protège que les salariés de quarante ans et plus ; en France et au Royaume-Uni, l'âge est protégé dans les deux sens. « Senior » en anglais évoque la hiérarchie, pas l'âge : dites « older workers ».

def: A long-term physical or mental condition that makes ordinary activities, including work, substantially harder.

formal.ex: The employee has disclosed a [[disability]] within the meaning of the applicable legislation.

everyday.ex: He has [[a health condition]] that makes long days at a screen difficult.

note_fr: « Handicap » est aujourd'hui jugé blessant en anglais lorsqu'il s'applique à une personne : dites « disability ». De même, évitez « invalid » et « handicapped ».

def: A member of staff who has a disability.

formal.ex: The employer shall take appropriate measures to enable a [[disabled employee]] to remain in work.
formal.ex_us: The employer shall take appropriate measures to enable an [[employee with a disability]] to remain in work.

everyday.ex: We've just changed the door system so that our [[disabled colleagues]] can get in on their own.
everyday.ex_us: We've just changed the door system so that our [[colleagues with disabilities]] can get in on their own.

note_fr: L'usage britannique préfère « disabled people » (modèle social du handicap), l'usage américain « people with disabilities » (la personne d'abord). Dans les deux pays, « the disabled » et « the handicapped » sont à proscrire.

def: The principle that people in comparable situations must be treated in the same way.

formal.ex: The measure is contrary to [[the principle of equal treatment]] between employees in a comparable situation.

everyday.ex: All we're asking managers to do is [[treat everyone the same]].

collocations: equal treatment of men and women
to be entitled to equal treatment
note_fr: En droit français, l'égalité de traitement est un principe général distinct de la non-discrimination : elle joue même sans critère prohibé. Cette distinction n'existe pas vraiment en droit britannique ou américain, où il faut rattacher la différence à un critère protégé.

def: The principle that everyone should have the same chance of being hired, trained and promoted, whatever their background.

formal.ex: The Company is committed to [[equality of opportunity]] at every stage of employment.
formal.ex_us: The Company is committed to [[equal employment opportunity]] at every stage of employment.

everyday.ex: We describe ourselves as an [[equal opportunities]] employer, so let's act like one.
everyday.ex_us: We describe ourselves as an [[equal opportunity]] employer, so let's act like one.

note_fr: Pluriel au Royaume-Uni (« equal opportunities »), singulier aux États-Unis (« equal opportunity », d'où le sigle EEO). Ne traduisez pas « chances » par « chances » : « equal chances » ne se dit pas dans ce sens.

def: To give someone worse conditions, chances or treatment than another person in a similar situation.

formal.ex: A part-time employee must not be [[treated less favourably]] than a comparable full-time employee.
formal.ex_us: A part-time employee must not be [[treated less favorably]] than a comparable full-time employee.

everyday.ex: Has she been [[treated differently]] from the rest of the team since she came back?

collocations: to be treated less favourably than a colleague
note_fr: « Less favourable treatment » est la formule légale de la discrimination directe ; « different treatment » est neutre et peut être parfaitement licite. Orthographe : favourably (UK), favorably (US).

def: Unwanted behaviour that offends, humiliates or intimidates another person.

formal.ex: Any employee found to have committed an act of [[harassment]] will be subject to disciplinary action.

everyday.ex: What she describes goes well beyond a clash of personalities; it's [[harassment]].

note_fr: Indénombrable : pas de « a harassment » ni de « harassments » ; dites « an act of harassment », « incidents of harassment ». Accent sur la première syllabe au Royaume-Uni, souvent sur la deuxième aux États-Unis. Au Royaume-Uni, « harassment » doit en droit être lié à un critère protégé.

def: To trouble, pressure or humiliate someone repeatedly.

formal.ex: No employee shall [[subject a colleague to harassment]] of any kind.

everyday.ex: She says he's been [[harassing]] her for months.

informal.ex: He's always [[picking on]] the new recruits.

collocations: to be harassed by one's manager
note_fr: « To harass » est plus fort que « to bother » ou « to pester » (importuner). « To pick on someone » = s'en prendre à quelqu'un, registre familier. Attention : « to harass » ne prend qu'un r et deux s.

def: Repeated behaviour at work that wears a person down, damages their working conditions and may harm their health, dignity or career.

formal.ex: Under French law, [[moral harassment]] consists of repeated acts which have the purpose or effect of degrading an employee's working conditions.

everyday.ex: Three people in his team have now complained about [[bullying]].

note_fr: « Moral harassment » est un calque que seuls comprennent les juristes habitués au droit français : à l'oral, dites « bullying ». Mais « bullying » n'est pas une notion légale au Royaume-Uni ni aux États-Unis : le harcèlement n'y est sanctionné en tant que tel que s'il est lié à un critère protégé.

explain.written: Harcèlement moral ('moral harassment') is a French legal concept covering repeated acts which have the purpose or effect of degrading an employee's working conditions in a way likely to infringe his or her rights and dignity, impair his or her physical or mental health or jeopardise his or her career; it is both a civil wrong and a criminal offence, whatever the reason behind it.
explain.spoken: It's what you'd call workplace bullying, except that in France it's a legal concept in its own right: it doesn't need to be linked to sex, race or anything else, and it can be a criminal offence.

def: Unwanted behaviour of a sexual nature, such as remarks, touching or pressure for sexual favours.

formal.ex: [[Sexual harassment]] is a criminal offence in France and constitutes serious misconduct.

everyday.ex: She came to see me about [[sexual harassment]] by a client.

collocations: sexual harassment by a third party
note_fr: En France, le harcèlement sexuel suppose en principe des propos ou comportements répétés, mais une pression grave exercée une seule fois pour obtenir un acte sexuel y est assimilée. Au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis, un seul incident suffisamment grave peut suffire.

def: Things said that are unsuitable at work because they are offensive, sexual or humiliating.

formal.ex: Several witnesses confirmed that [[offensive remarks]] had been made about her accent.
formal.ex_us: Several witnesses confirmed that [[offensive comments]] had been made about her accent.

everyday.ex: He keeps making [[inappropriate remarks]] about what she wears.
everyday.ex_us: He keeps making [[inappropriate comments]] about what she wears.

informal.ex: That joke in the meeting was completely [[out of order]].
informal.ex_us: That joke in the meeting was completely [[out of line]].

collocations: to make a remark about someone
note_fr: « Déplacé » ne se traduit pas par « displaced » ni « misplaced » : dites « inappropriate ». On « makes » a remark (jamais « does » ni « says »). « Out of order » (UK) / « out of line » (US) = qui dépasse les bornes.

def: Conduct that is not acceptable in a professional setting.

formal.ex: The investigation concerns allegations of [[inappropriate conduct]] at the annual sales conference.

everyday.ex: There have been a few reports of [[inappropriate behaviour]] at the Christmas party.
everyday.ex_us: There have been a few reports of [[inappropriate behavior]] at the holiday party.

note_fr: « Behaviour » est indénombrable dans cet emploi : « this behaviour », pas « these behaviours » (pluriel réservé au jargon RH). « Conduct » est le terme des textes et des rapports ; « agissements » se rend par « acts » ou « conduct ».

def: To be made to experience something unpleasant.

formal.ex: No employee shall [[be subjected to]] repeated acts of harassment.

everyday.uk: to be on the receiving end of
everyday.us: to be on the receiving end of
everyday.ex: She's been [[on the receiving end of]] his sarcasm for over a year.

note_fr: « Subir » ne se traduit pas par « to undergo » (réservé aux examens, opérations, changements) ni par « to suffer from » (une maladie). Ne confondez pas « to be subjected to » (subir) et « to be subject to » (être soumis à).

def: A statement, made to the employer, that something wrong or unfair has happened.

formal.ex: On 3 March, the Company received a [[formal complaint]] of harassment from a member of the finance team.

everyday.ex: We've had a [[complaint]] about one of the team leaders.

note_fr: « Complaint » couvre à la fois le signalement interne et la plainte en justice ; le contexte tranche. « Plainte » au sens pénal français se dit « criminal complaint ». « A complaint OF harassment » (objet), « a complaint ABOUT a manager » (personne visée).

fr: faire un signalement / déposer une plainte
def: To tell the employer, officially, that you have been treated wrongly.

formal.ex: Any employee may [[lodge a complaint]] with the Human Resources Department.
formal.ex_us: Any employee may [[file a complaint]] with the Human Resources Department.

everyday.ex: She's thinking about [[making a complaint]], but she's worried about how it'll look.
everyday.ex_us: She's thinking about [[filing a complaint]], but she's worried about how it'll look.

informal.ex: In the end he [[put in a complaint]] to HR.

collocations: to complain to HR about a manager
to lodge a complaint with the Defender of Rights
note_fr: On ne dit pas « to deposit a complaint » ni « to do a complaint ». « To lodge » est britannique et soutenu, « to file » est la forme américaine courante. On « complains TO someone ABOUT something ».

def: A formal complaint that an employee raises with the employer about the way he or she has been treated.

formal.ex: The employee submitted a [[formal grievance]] under the Company's grievance procedure.
formal.ex_us: The employee submitted a [[formal internal complaint]] under the Company's complaint procedure.

everyday.us: to file a complaint with HR
everyday.ex: If the chat with her manager doesn't sort it out, she can always [[raise a grievance]].
everyday.ex_us: If the talk with her manager doesn't fix it, she can always [[file a complaint with HR]].

note_fr: « Grievance » est le terme britannique consacré : toute entreprise y a une « grievance procedure », avec audition et recours interne. Aux États-Unis, « grievance » évoque surtout la procédure prévue par une convention syndicale. La France n'a pas de procédure légale équivalente.

def: The person who makes a complaint.

formal.ex: [[The complainant]] was interviewed on two occasions and given the opportunity to comment on the notes.

everyday.uk: the person who made the complaint
everyday.us: the person who filed the complaint
everyday.ex: Have we told [[the person who made the complaint]] what happens next?
everyday.ex_us: Have we told [[the person who filed the complaint]] what happens next?

note_fr: Préférez « complainant » à « victim » dans un rapport d'enquête : tant que les faits ne sont pas établis, « victim » préjuge de la conclusion (au besoin, « alleged victim »). « Plaintiff » ou « claimant » désignent le demandeur devant un tribunal.

def: The person against whom a complaint has been made.

formal.ex: [[The respondent]] denied each of the allegations put to him.

everyday.ex: We also have a duty towards [[the person complained about]].
everyday.ex_us: We also have a duty toward [[the person accused]].

note_fr: Il n'existe pas d'équivalent court de « mis en cause » : selon le document, « the respondent », « the alleged harasser » ou « the person complained about ». Évitez « the accused » (procès pénal) et « the harasser » sans « alleged » tant que rien n'est établi.

def: A person who saw or heard what happened and can describe it.

formal.ex: Each [[witness]] was reminded that the content of the interview must remain confidential.

everyday.ex: Were there any [[witnesses]], or is it her word against his?

note_fr: « Witness » est aussi un verbe : « Did you witness the incident? ». Ne dites pas « to assist to a scene » : « to assist » signifie aider. « Her word against his » = parole contre parole.

def: A statement that someone has done something wrong, which has not yet been proved.

formal.ex: The [[allegations]] were put to the respondent in writing before the interview.

everyday.ex: Before we go any further, I need to be clear about [[what is being alleged]].

collocations: to make an allegation against someone
to put the allegations to someone
note_fr: « Allegation » n'a rien de péjoratif : c'est le mot neutre pour des faits dénoncés mais non établis. L'adjectif « alleged » et l'adverbe « allegedly » sont indispensables dans tout écrit d'enquête (« the alleged incident »).

def: A fact-finding process run by or for the employer to establish what happened after a complaint.

formal.ex: The Company has decided to open an [[internal investigation]] into the matters raised.
formal.ex_us: The Company has decided to open a [[workplace investigation]] into the matters raised.

everyday.ex: The [[investigation]] should take about three weeks.

note_fr: Faux ami : « inquiry » ou « enquiry » désigne plutôt une demande de renseignements ou une enquête publique ; pour l'entreprise, dites « investigation ». Préposition : « an investigation INTO », jamais « on » ni « about ».

def: To try to find out the facts about something.

formal.ex: The employer is under a duty to [[investigate]] any report of harassment promptly.

everyday.ex: Leave it with me; I'll [[look into]] it this week.

informal.uk: to get to the bottom of
informal.us: to get to the bottom of
informal.ex: We need to [[get to the bottom of]] what happened on that trip.

note_fr: « To investigate » est transitif : « to investigate a complaint », sans préposition (pas « investigate on »). « To look into » est l'équivalent oral naturel ; « to enquire about » signifie seulement se renseigner.

def: The person appointed to establish the facts of a complaint.

formal.ex: The [[investigating officer]] shall have had no prior involvement in the matter.
formal.ex_us: The [[investigator]] shall have had no prior involvement in the matter.

everyday.ex: We've brought in an outside [[investigator]] because the manager concerned reports to the HR Director.

note_fr: « Investigating officer » est l'expression des procédures britanniques. En France, l'enquête est souvent menée en binôme (direction et représentant du personnel) : « a joint investigation ». « Inquisitor » n'est évidemment pas le mot.

def: A meeting in which the investigator questions the complainant, the respondent or a witness.

formal.ex: You are invited to attend an [[investigation interview]] on Thursday 14 May at 10 a.m.
formal.ex_us: You are asked to attend an [[investigatory interview]] on Thursday, May 14, at 10 a.m.

everyday.ex: We still need to [[interview]] two people from the night shift.

collocations: to take notes of the interview
to be accompanied at the interview
note_fr: N'employez pas « audition » (réservé aux comédiens et musiciens) ni « hearing », qui désigne au Royaume-Uni la réunion où l'on statue (« grievance hearing », « disciplinary hearing »). L'entretien d'enquête sert seulement à établir les faits.

def: Facts, documents or statements that help to show whether something is true.

formal.ex: The investigator found no [[evidence]] to support the second allegation.

everyday.ex: Is there [[something to go on]] - emails, messages, anything in writing?

collocations: to back up a claim with evidence
note_fr: Indénombrable : jamais « an evidence » ni « evidences » ; dites « a piece of evidence », « some evidence ». « Proof » est plus fort (preuve certaine). Faux ami : « evidence » ne signifie pas « évidence ».

def: To make sure that information is shared only with the people who need to know it.

formal.uk: to treat in the strictest confidence
formal.us: to treat in the strictest confidence
formal.ex: All statements will be [[treated in the strictest confidence]], subject to the requirements of the investigation.

everyday.ex: Please [[keep this conversation confidential]] - that includes your team.

informal.ex: I'd ask you to [[keep this to yourself]] for now.

note_fr: Ne promettez jamais une confidentialité absolue : la personne mise en cause doit connaître les faits reprochés. La formule honnête est « on a need-to-know basis ». Faux ami : « confidence » = confiance ; « in confidence » = sous le sceau du secret.

def: To tell someone in authority that something wrong has happened.

formal.ex: Employees are encouraged to [[report]] any conduct that may breach this policy.

everyday.ex: Thanks for [[flagging]] this - you did the right thing.

collocations: to report a concern to HR
note_fr: « To signal » ne s'emploie pas dans ce sens. « To report someone » = dénoncer quelqu'un, sans nuance péjorative ; « to denounce » est politique ou moral et sonne faux en entreprise. « To raise a concern » est la formule la plus douce.

def: To say openly that something is wrong instead of staying silent.

formal.ex: Employees who [[raise a concern]] in good faith will be supported by the Company.

everyday.ex: It took her a year to [[speak up]], which tells you something about the culture.

collocations: to feel safe to speak up
note_fr: « To speak up » = oser signaler en interne ; « to speak out » = prendre position publiquement. Les entreprises anglo-saxonnes parlent de « speak-up culture » là où le français dit « libération de la parole ».

def: Punishing someone, openly or not, because they complained or helped with a complaint.

formal.ex: [[Retaliation]] against any person who reports harassment in good faith is strictly prohibited.

everyday.uk: to take it out on someone
everyday.us: to take it out on someone
everyday.ex: I don't want him [[taking it out on her]] once he knows who complained.

informal.ex: Moving her desk to the basement looks a lot like [[payback]].

note_fr: Terme central aux États-Unis, où les plaintes pour « retaliation » sont les plus nombreuses devant l'EEOC. Le droit britannique parle de « victimisation ». « Reprisals » existe mais sonne militaire ; « revenge » est personnel et non juridique.

def: A person who reports wrongdoing they have learned about, usually at work.

formal.ex: A [[whistleblower]] who reports in good faith may not be dismissed or penalised for doing so.

everyday.ex: He [[blew the whistle]] on the way overtime was being recorded.

collocations: to blow the whistle on something
note_fr: « To blow the whistle ON something » (préposition « on »). Le mot est neutre, voire positif ; évitez « informer » ou « snitch », qui signifient délateur. Chaque pays a sa propre définition légale : ne présumez pas que le statut français s'applique ailleurs.

fr: écart de rémunération entre les femmes et les hommes
def: The difference between the average pay of men and of women in an organisation or a country.

formal.ex: The report shows a median [[gender pay gap]] of eight per cent across the group.

everyday.ex: The [[pay gap]] is mostly down to who holds the senior jobs.

collocations: to close the gender pay gap
the mean and median pay gap
note_fr: Ne confondez pas « gender pay gap » (écart moyen, tous postes confondus) et « equal pay » (même salaire pour un même travail) : une entreprise peut respecter le second et afficher un écart important. Au Royaume-Uni, la publication de l'écart est obligatoire pour les employeurs de 250 salariés et plus.

def: The right of men and women to receive the same pay for the same or equivalent work.

formal.ex: The employer shall ensure [[equal pay]] between women and men for the same work or for work of equal value.

everyday.ex: Are the two of them [[paid the same]] for what is basically the same job?

note_fr: Aux États-Unis, on parle aussi de « pay equity ». « Equal salary » est compris mais n'est pas l'expression consacrée. En anglais, on dit « women and men » ou « men and women », jamais « the women and the men ».

def: Policies aimed at employing people from varied backgrounds and making sure they are all able to contribute and progress.

formal.ex: The Board reviews the Group's [[equality, diversity and inclusion]] strategy once a year.
formal.ex_us: The Board reviews the Group's [[diversity, equity and inclusion]] strategy once a year.

everyday.ex: She heads up [[diversity and inclusion]] for the whole of Europe.

informal.ex: The [[D&I]] team is running a session on inclusive hiring.
informal.ex_us: The [[DEI]] team is running a session on inclusive hiring.

note_fr: Sigles : EDI ou D&I au Royaume-Uni, DEI aux États-Unis, où le sujet est devenu politiquement très sensible. « Equity » (équité) n'est pas « equality » (égalité). « Diverse » se dit d'un groupe, jamais d'une personne.

def: A policy of acting on every case of unacceptable behaviour, however minor it seems.

formal.ex: The Company operates a [[zero-tolerance approach]] to harassment of any kind.

everyday.ex: We say we have [[zero tolerance]], and then we promote the people everyone complains about.

collocations: to take a firm line on harassment
note_fr: Trait d'union lorsque l'expression est épithète : « a zero-tolerance policy ». Attention : « zero tolerance » ne signifie pas sanction automatique ; chaque cas doit rester examiné individuellement.

def: To treat a complaint as important and act on it properly.

formal.uk: to give a complaint due consideration
formal.us: to give a complaint due consideration
formal.ex: The Company will [[give every complaint due consideration]], regardless of the seniority of the person concerned.

everyday.ex: I want you to know that we [[take your complaint very seriously]].

informal.ex: Her manager just [[brushed it off]] and told her not to be so sensitive.

collocations: to follow up on a complaint
to dismiss a complaint out of hand
to sweep something under the carpet
note_fr: « To brush off » et « to sweep under the carpet » (US : « under the rug ») décrivent l'attitude inverse : balayer, étouffer l'affaire. « To take seriously » se construit sans « in » : pas de « take in serious ».

def: A voluntary process in which a neutral person helps two people in conflict to reach their own solution.

formal.ex: With the agreement of both parties, the matter may be referred to [[mediation]].

everyday.uk: to sit down with a mediator
everyday.us: to sit down with a mediator
everyday.ex: Would the two of them be willing to [[sit down with a mediator]]?

note_fr: La médiation suppose l'accord des deux parties et ne convient pas aux faits graves : ne la proposez jamais comme substitut à l'enquête en cas de harcèlement sexuel présumé. En France, le Code du travail prévoit une procédure de médiation en matière de harcèlement moral.

def: Treating one person less well than another in a comparable situation because of a protected ground.

formal.ex: Refusing to promote an employee because she is pregnant constitutes [[direct discrimination]].
formal.ex_us: Refusing to promote an employee because she is pregnant constitutes [[disparate treatment]].

everyday.uk: to treat someone worse because of
everyday.us: to treat someone worse because of
everyday.ex: Put simply, he was [[treated worse because of]] his age.

note_fr: Le droit français et le droit britannique disent « direct discrimination » ; le droit américain parle de « disparate treatment », qui suppose en principe une intention. Ne confondez pas « disparate treatment » et « disparate impact ».

def: A rule that looks neutral and applies to everyone, but in practice puts one protected group at a particular disadvantage without good reason.

formal.ex: A requirement to work full time may give rise to [[indirect discrimination]] against women unless it can be objectively justified.
formal.ex_us: A requirement to work full time may give rise to a [[disparate impact]] on women unless it is justified by business necessity.

everyday.uk: to put a group at a disadvantage
everyday.us: to put a group at a disadvantage
everyday.ex: The rule is the same for everyone, but it clearly [[puts part-timers at a disadvantage]].

collocations: to put at a particular disadvantage
note_fr: Notion statistique plus que morale : aucune intention n'est requise. Le droit américain parle de « disparate impact » ou d'« adverse impact ». Dites « apparently neutral », pas « neutral in appearance ».

def: In British law, the nine personal attributes on which discrimination is prohibited, such as age, disability, race and sex.

formal.ex: Harassment is unwanted conduct related to a relevant [[protected characteristic]].

everyday.uk: to be covered by the Equality Act
everyday.us: to be covered by the Equality Act
everyday.ex: Being a smoker isn't [[covered by the Equality Act]], so it isn't discrimination in the legal sense.

collocations: one of the nine protected characteristics
note_fr: Expression propre à l'Equality Act 2010 britannique, qui retient neuf critères : âge, handicap, changement de sexe, mariage et partenariat civil, grossesse et maternité, race, religion ou convictions, sexe, orientation sexuelle. Aux États-Unis, on parle de « protected classes » ; en France, de « critères » ou « motifs » prohibés, nettement plus nombreux.

def: In US law, the groups of people whom anti-discrimination statutes protect, defined by characteristics such as race, sex, religion, national origin, age or disability.

formal.ex: The plaintiff must show that she is a member of a [[protected class]].

everyday.uk: to be in a protected class
everyday.us: to be in a protected class
everyday.ex: Everyone [[is in a protected class]] in one way or another - we all have a race and a sex.

collocations: a member of a protected class
note_fr: Terminologie américaine : la liste fédérale est complétée, parfois très largement, par les lois des États et des villes. « Class » ne renvoie pas ici à la classe sociale. Au Royaume-Uni, on dit « protected characteristics ».

fr: discrimination liée à la grossesse et à la maternité
def: Unfavourable treatment of a woman because she is pregnant, has given birth or is on maternity leave.

formal.ex: Withholding a pay rise from an employee on maternity leave may amount to [[pregnancy and maternity discrimination]].
formal.ex_us: Withholding a raise from an employee on maternity leave may amount to [[pregnancy discrimination]].

everyday.uk: to be sidelined after maternity leave
everyday.us: to be sidelined after maternity leave
everyday.ex: She came back to find she'd been [[sidelined after maternity leave]]: her best clients had gone to someone else.

note_fr: « Pregnant » se dit sans détour en anglais ; évitez « in a family way » ou « expecting » dans un écrit. « Pay rise » (UK) = « raise » (US). « To sideline » = mettre sur la touche.

fr: orientation sexuelle et identité de genre
def: Whom a person is attracted to, and a person's own sense of being male, female or neither; both are protected grounds.

formal.ex: The policy prohibits discrimination on the grounds of [[sexual orientation and gender identity]].

everyday.ex: We've set up a network for [[LGBT+ colleagues]] and allies.
everyday.ex_us: We've set up a network for [[LGBTQ+ colleagues]] and allies.

note_fr: « Gender » (genre) n'est pas « sex » (sexe) : les textes britanniques distinguent « sex », « sexual orientation » et « gender reassignment ». « Transgender » est un adjectif, jamais un nom : « a transgender employee », pas « a transgender ».

def: A person's faith or philosophical convictions, or lack of them, as a protected ground.

formal.ex: No employee shall be treated less favourably on the grounds of [[religion or belief]].
formal.ex_us: No employee shall be treated less favorably on the basis of [[religion]].

everyday.ex: We try to plan team events around [[people's faith]] - not everything has to happen in a bar.

note_fr: La laïcité à la française n'a pas d'équivalent : au Royaume-Uni et plus encore aux États-Unis, l'employeur doit en principe s'adapter aux pratiques religieuses (« religious accommodation ») sauf contrainte excessive. Une clause de neutralité dans un règlement intérieur surprend beaucoup un interlocuteur américain : expliquez-la.

def: Any conduct related to a person's sex that undermines their dignity or creates an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment.

formal.ex: The internal rules must reproduce the statutory provisions on harassment and [[sexist conduct]].

everyday.ex: Calling the women in the team 'the girls' is exactly the kind of [[sexist behaviour]] the policy is aimed at.
everyday.ex_us: Calling the women on the team 'the girls' is exactly the kind of [[sexist behavior]] the policy is aimed at.

informal.ex: There's a lot of [[casual sexism]] in that department that nobody ever challenges.

note_fr: L'agissement sexiste est une notion du Code du travail français, distincte du harcèlement sexuel : un acte isolé suffit. Au Royaume-Uni, de tels faits relèvent du « harassment related to sex ». « Casual sexism » = sexisme ordinaire.

explain.written: An agissement sexiste ('sexist conduct') is defined in the French Labour Code as any conduct related to a person's sex which has the purpose or effect of violating that person's dignity or of creating an intimidating, hostile, degrading, humiliating or offensive environment; a single act is sufficient.
explain.spoken: French law has a specific category for sexist behaviour that isn't sexual harassment - a single sexist remark can be enough, and the employer has to act on it.

def: Behaviour that the person on the receiving end has not invited and does not want.

formal.ex: Harassment is defined as [[unwanted conduct]] which has the purpose or effect of violating a person's dignity.
formal.ex_us: Harassment is defined as [[unwelcome conduct]] that is severe or pervasive enough to create an abusive working environment.

everyday.ex: She's made it clear more than once that it's [[unwanted attention]].
everyday.ex_us: She's made it clear more than once that it's [[unwelcome attention]].

collocations: to make it clear that the conduct is unwanted
note_fr: « Unwanted » est le terme de la loi britannique, « unwelcome » celui de la pratique américaine. La victime n'a pas à avoir protesté expressément pour que le comportement soit « unwanted ». « Undesired » ne s'emploie pas ici.

def: Attempts to start a sexual or romantic relationship with someone.

formal.ex: The complainant states that she was subjected to [[unwelcome sexual advances]] during the business trip.

everyday.ex: He [[came on to her]] at the leaving drinks and wouldn't take no for an answer.

informal.uk: to make a pass at someone
informal.us: to make a pass at someone
informal.ex: Apparently he [[made a pass at]] one of the interns.

collocations: to make advances to a colleague
to take no for an answer
note_fr: Dans ce sens, toujours au pluriel : « advances ». Rien à voir avec « an advance » (avance sur salaire). « To come on to » et « to make a pass at » sont familiers : ils conviennent pour rapporter des propos, pas pour un rapport.

def: Sexual harassment in which a job benefit is promised, or a threat made, in exchange for sexual favours.

formal.ex: Making a promotion conditional on sexual favours is the classic example of [[quid pro quo harassment]].

everyday.ex: He [[abused his position]] to pressure her into seeing him outside work.

note_fr: Expression surtout américaine, opposée au « hostile work environment ». En droit français, l'équivalent est la « pression grave » exercée dans le but d'obtenir un acte de nature sexuelle, constituée même sans répétition.

def: In US law, a workplace where unwelcome conduct based on a protected characteristic is so severe or pervasive that it changes the conditions of employment.

formal.ex: To establish a [[hostile work environment]], the conduct must be severe or pervasive.

everyday.ex: Nobody is being targeted personally; it's the whole [[toxic atmosphere]] on that floor.

note_fr: Notion juridique américaine précise : la simple mauvaise ambiance ou un chef désagréable ne suffisent pas ; il faut un lien avec un critère protégé et des faits « severe or pervasive ». Les salariés l'emploient souvent à tort. La jurisprudence française connaît une idée voisine, le harcèlement « d'ambiance ».

def: Joking and teasing between colleagues, often used as an excuse for remarks that are in fact offensive.

formal.ex: The respondent described the remarks as [[comments presented as humour]] which were not intended to offend.
formal.ex_us: The respondent described the remarks as [[comments presented as humor]] that were not intended to offend.

everyday.ex: He says it was just [[banter]]; she says it happened every single day.
everyday.ex_us: He says they were just [[joking around]]; she says it happened every single day.

informal.ex: 'It was only [[a bit of a laugh]]' is not a defence.
informal.ex_us: 'We were [[just kidding around]]' is not a defense.

collocations: to go along with a joke
note_fr: « Banter » est très britannique ; la défense « it was just banter » échoue régulièrement devant les tribunaux. C'est l'effet du propos qui compte, pas l'intention affichée. « To laugh it off » = faire mine d'en rire.

def: To make someone feel small or unimportant, especially in front of others.

formal.ex: The respondent repeatedly [[demeaned]] the complainant in front of clients.

everyday.ex: He [[belittles]] her in every team meeting, usually with a smile.

informal.ex: She's forever [[putting him down]] in front of the juniors.

note_fr: « To undermine » (saper l'autorité ou la confiance) est très fréquent dans les signalements : « I feel constantly undermined ». « To denigrate » existe mais reste littéraire. « To talk down to » = parler avec condescendance.

def: To push someone away from the work, meetings or information that matter.

formal.ex: The complainant alleges that she was deliberately [[excluded]] from meetings relevant to her role.

everyday.ex: Since the reorganisation he's been completely [[sidelined]].

informal.ex: The rest of the team have [[frozen her out]] since she complained.

collocations: to be left out of meetings
to give someone the cold shoulder
note_fr: Le « placard » français n'a pas d'équivalent imagé : « to be sidelined » ou « to be frozen out ». « To ostracise » (US : ostracize) appartient au registre soutenu. Ne dites pas « to put in a cupboard ».

def: A series of similar acts over time, as opposed to a single incident.

formal.ex: Moral harassment requires [[repeated acts]]; a single incident, however serious, is not sufficient.

everyday.ex: One sharp email proves nothing, but twelve in a month looks like a [[pattern of behaviour]].
everyday.ex_us: One sharp email proves nothing, but twelve in a month looks like a [[pattern of behavior]].

note_fr: « A one-off » (UK) ou « an isolated incident » = un fait isolé. « Pattern » est le mot juste là où le français dit « caractère répété » ; « repetition » sonne scolaire.

def: Using a position of power in a way that goes beyond what the job legitimately requires.

formal.ex: The acts complained of go beyond the normal exercise of managerial powers and constitute an [[abuse of authority]].

everyday.ex: There's firm management, and then there's [[throwing your weight around]].

collocations: the normal exercise of managerial authority
note_fr: La ligne de partage, dans les trois pays : « firm management » ou « legitimate management action » n'est pas du harcèlement. « Abuse » se prononce avec /s/ pour le nom et /z/ pour le verbe. « To overstep the mark » = dépasser les bornes.

term.uk: to turn a blind eye to
term.us: to turn a blind eye to

def: To know that something wrong is happening and choose to do nothing about it.

formal.ex: A manager who fails to act may be regarded as having [[condoned]] the behaviour.

everyday.uk: to turn a blind eye to
everyday.us: to turn a blind eye to
everyday.ex: Management has been [[turning a blind eye to]] this for years because he brings in the big accounts.

informal.ex: Everybody knew, and everybody [[looked the other way]].

note_fr: « To condone » = tolérer, cautionner par son silence : mot clé des rapports d'enquête. « An open secret » = un secret de Polichinelle. Ne dites pas « to close the eyes on ».

def: Someone who sees unacceptable behaviour without being directly involved in it.

formal.ex: The training encourages [[bystanders]] to intervene or to report what they have seen.

everyday.ex: There must be [[someone who saw it happen]] and is willing to say so.

collocations: to stand by and do nothing
note_fr: Les formations « active bystander » sont devenues courantes au Royaume-Uni et aux États-Unis. Ne confondez pas avec « witness » (qui témoigne des faits dans l'enquête) ni avec « standby » (attente).

def: To offer information or make a complaint of one's own accord.

formal.ex: Employees who have relevant information are invited to [[come forward]] in confidence.

everyday.ex: Two more women have [[come forward]] since the investigation started.

collocations: to come forward as a witness
to be reluctant to come forward
note_fr: Verbe à particule valable à l'écrit comme à l'oral. « To manifest oneself » est un calque qui ne veut rien dire ici. « Reluctant to come forward » = qui hésite à parler.

def: To pass a problem up to a more senior person or a more formal stage.

formal.ex: If the concern involves a director, the HR Department shall [[refer the matter to]] the Group Compliance Officer.

everyday.ex: If it happens again, [[escalate]] it straight to me.

informal.ex: I've tried talking to him; I'm going to have to [[take it higher up]].

note_fr: « To escalate » est transitif dans le jargon d'entreprise : « to escalate an issue ». Pas de calque du type « to make it go up ». Attention, « the situation escalated » signifie aussi que la situation s'est envenimée.

fr: référent harcèlement sexuel et agissements sexistes
def: A person appointed to guide, inform and support employees on sexual harassment and sexist behaviour.

formal.uk: sexual harassment and sexist conduct officer
formal.us: sexual harassment and sexist conduct officer
formal.ex: The works council shall appoint a [[sexual harassment and sexist conduct officer]] from among its members.

everyday.ex: If you'd rather not go to your manager, you can talk to the [[harassment officer]].

note_fr: Notion française. En France, le CSE désigne un référent parmi ses membres, et les entreprises d'au moins 250 salariés en nomment un de leur côté. Les entreprises britanniques ont parfois des « harassment advisers » ou « dignity at work contacts », sans obligation légale.

explain.written: The référent harcèlement is a designated officer, required by the French Labour Code, whose role is to guide, inform and support employees in matters of sexual harassment and sexist conduct; one is appointed by the works council from among its members and, in larger companies, another by the employer.
explain.spoken: It's a designated point of contact for sexual harassment - someone on the works council, and in bigger companies someone on the employer's side too, that staff can go to for advice and support.

def: The independent French authority that, among other things, helps victims of discrimination and guides whistleblowers.

formal.ex: The employee has referred the matter to [[the Defender of Rights]], which has asked the Company for its observations.

everyday.ex: She's taken it to [[the French equality watchdog]], so expect a letter asking for our side of the story.

collocations: to refer a matter to the Defender of Rights
note_fr: Gardez le nom français à la première mention, suivi de la traduction entre parenthèses. Son rôle se rapproche de celui de l'EHRC britannique ou de l'EEOC américaine, mais sa saisine est gratuite, facultative et n'est jamais un préalable au procès.

explain.written: The Défenseur des droits (Defender of Rights) is an independent French constitutional authority which any person may approach free of charge; it investigates complaints of discrimination, may make recommendations and submit observations to the courts, and also guides and protects whistleblowers.
explain.spoken: It's an independent public body - a bit like an ombudsman for discrimination. Anyone can go to it for free; it can investigate, ask the employer for explanations and give its view to the court.

fr: EEOC (agence fédérale américaine de lutte contre les discriminations au travail)
def: The US federal agency that enforces the federal laws against discrimination at work.

formal.ex: An employee must generally file a charge with [[the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission]] before bringing a lawsuit under federal law.

everyday.ex: She's gone to [[the EEOC]], so we need to preserve every document.

collocations: to file a charge with the EEOC
note_fr: On épelle le sigle : « the E-E-O-C ». Différence majeure avec la France : aux États-Unis, la saisine de l'agence (« charge ») est en principe un préalable obligatoire à l'action en justice fondée sur le droit fédéral.

fr: EHRC (autorité britannique de l'égalité et des droits de l'homme)
def: The public body that promotes and enforces equality law in Great Britain.

formal.uk: the Equality and Human Rights Commission
formal.us: the Equality and Human Rights Commission
formal.ex: The policy has been drafted in the light of the guidance published by [[the Equality and Human Rights Commission]].

everyday.ex: [[The EHRC]] has published technical guidance on harassment at work that's well worth reading.

note_fr: À la différence de l'EEOC ou du Défenseur des droits, l'EHRC ne traite pas les réclamations individuelles : le salarié britannique saisit l'employment tribunal, après une tentative de conciliation auprès de l'Acas. L'EHRC publie des guides et peut agir contre les employeurs.

def: To bring a complaint formally before an official body so that it can deal with it.

formal.ex: Any person who believes they have suffered discrimination may [[refer the matter to]] the Defender of Rights.
formal.ex_us: Any person who believes they have suffered discrimination may [[file a charge with]] the EEOC.

everyday.ex: If we get this wrong, she'll [[take it to]] the labour inspector.
everyday.ex_us: If we get this wrong, she'll [[take it to]] the labor inspector.

collocations: to bring a complaint before an authority
to refer the matter to the labour inspectorate
to file a charge of discrimination
note_fr: « Saisir » n'a pas d'équivalent unique : « to refer a matter to », « to bring a complaint before », « to apply to » selon l'organe. « To seize » signifie saisir au sens matériel (confisquer). « To file a charge » ne vaut que pour l'EEOC et les agences américaines.

fr: politique de lutte contre le harcèlement
def: A written document setting out what behaviour is forbidden, how to complain and what the employer will do.

formal.ex: This [[anti-harassment and bullying policy]] applies to all employees, contractors and visitors.
formal.ex_us: This [[anti-harassment policy]] applies to all employees, contractors and visitors.

everyday.ex: Have a look at the [[dignity at work policy]] - it tells you exactly who to go to.
everyday.ex_us: Take a look at the [[respectful workplace policy]] - it tells you exactly who to go to.

note_fr: « Policy » = règle ou charte interne, pas « politique » au sens général, ni « police ». « Dignity at work policy » est l'intitulé britannique usuel. En France, les dispositions légales sur le harcèlement doivent figurer dans le règlement intérieur (« internal rules »).

def: The route - a person, an email address, a phone line or an online platform - by which staff can report wrongdoing.

formal.ex: The Company has established an [[internal reporting channel]] for the receipt and handling of reports.

everyday.ex: You can also use the [[speak-up line]], which is run by an outside provider.
everyday.ex_us: You can also use the [[ethics hotline]], which is run by an outside vendor.

collocations: to report through the proper channels
to acknowledge receipt of a report
note_fr: En France, les entreprises d'au moins cinquante salariés doivent mettre en place une procédure interne de recueil des signalements. « Channel » se prononce /ˈtʃæn(ə)l/. « Alert line » est un calque : dites « hotline », « helpline » ou « speak-up line ».

def: Information about wrongdoing given by someone who does not reveal their identity.

formal.ex: An [[anonymous report]] will be investigated in so far as it contains sufficiently detailed information.

everyday.ex: She's willing to tell us what she saw, but she wants to [[stay anonymous]].

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « anonymous » (l'employeur ignore qui parle) et « confidential » (il le sait mais ne le divulgue pas). Un témoignage anonyme a une faible valeur probante devant le juge français. « A tip-off » = un tuyau, registre familier.

def: Honestly believing that what one reports is true, even if it later turns out to be mistaken.

formal.ex: No action will be taken against an employee who reports a concern [[in good faith]], even if the concern proves to be unfounded.

everyday.ex: Even if she got some of it wrong, she [[genuinely believed]] what she was telling us.

collocations: a complaint made in good faith
note_fr: « In good faith », sans article ; le contraire est « in bad faith ». En droit français, seul le salarié de mauvaise foi, c'est-à-dire qui sait les faits faux, perd la protection : une plainte simplement non établie ne suffit pas.

def: A complaint made by someone who knows it to be untrue, in order to harm another person.

formal.ex: The making of a [[malicious or vexatious complaint]] may itself give rise to disciplinary action.
formal.ex_us: The filing of a [[knowingly false complaint]] may itself give rise to disciplinary action.

everyday.ex: There's nothing to suggest she [[made it up]].

collocations: to make an allegation knowing it to be false
note_fr: « Malicious » = malveillant (et non malicieux, espiègle). « Vexatious » = abusif, fait pour nuire. Ne laissez pas un client assimiler « unsubstantiated » (non établi) et « malicious » (mensonger) : c'est l'erreur qui coûte le plus cher.

def: Temporary steps taken to protect the people involved while the investigation is under way.

formal.ex: The Company may take [[interim measures]] to protect the parties, which shall not constitute a disciplinary sanction.

everyday.ex: [[In the meantime]], he'll report to Sarah and work from the other site.

collocations: pending the outcome of the investigation
a temporary change of reporting line
note_fr: « Conservatory » désigne une véranda ou un conservatoire de musique : dites « interim », « precautionary » ou « protective measures ». « Pending » = dans l'attente de. Veillez à ce que la mesure ne pénalise pas la personne qui s'est plainte.

def: To arrange work so that the complainant and the respondent are not in contact during the investigation.

formal.ex: It was decided to [[separate the parties]] for the duration of the investigation.

everyday.ex: Can we [[keep them apart]] without moving her? She's the one who complained.

collocations: to move someone to another team
note_fr: « The parties » désigne ici la personne plaignante et la personne mise en cause ; « protagonists » est théâtral. Règle d'or à savoir formuler : « It shouldn't be the complainant who pays the price ».

def: To record in writing what a person says they saw, heard or experienced.

formal.ex: The investigator [[took a witness statement]] from each of the six members of the team.

everyday.ex: I'd like to [[get your account]] of what happened at the offsite.

note_fr: « Testimony » se dit devant un tribunal ; dans une enquête interne, on parle de « statement » ou d'« account ». En France, l'attestation produite en justice obéit à un formalisme propre, sans équivalent exact : « a formal witness statement in the form required by French civil procedure ».

def: To confirm what someone has said by providing independent support for it.

formal.ex: The complainant's account is [[corroborated]] by contemporaneous text messages.

everyday.ex: Is there anything that [[backs up]] her version - emails, messages, a diary?

informal.ex: His story doesn't [[check out]]: he wasn't even in the office that day.

collocations: to tally with what others said
note_fr: « To back up » se sépare avec un pronom : « back it up ». « It tallies with » = cela concorde avec. « To bear out » (corroborer, confirmer) est un verbe à particule élégant, y compris à l'écrit.

def: What the investigator decides, on the evidence, did or did not happen.

formal.ex: The investigator's [[findings of fact]] are set out in section 4 of the report.

everyday.ex: We should have the [[findings]] by the end of the month.

note_fr: Distinguez « findings » (les faits tenus pour établis) et « recommendations » (les suites proposées). « Conclusions » existe, mais « findings » est le terme des rapports d'enquête. On « makes » ou « reaches » a finding.

def: The written document recording how the investigation was run, the evidence gathered and the conclusions reached.

formal.ex: The [[investigation report]] was submitted to the Managing Director on 12 June.

everyday.ex: I'll [[write it up]] over the weekend and send you a draft on Monday.

collocations: to share the report on a need-to-know basis
note_fr: « To write up » = mettre au propre, rédiger à partir de notes. En France, le rapport d'enquête interne peut être produit devant le juge, qui en apprécie librement la valeur probante : rédigez-le en pensant à ce lecteur.

fr: faire droit à la plainte / reconnaître les faits établis
def: To decide, after investigation, that the complaint is well founded.

formal.ex: The complaint was [[upheld]] in part.
formal.ex_us: The complaint was [[substantiated]] in part.

everyday.us: to find that the complaint was valid
everyday.ex: They [[found in her favour]] on two of the three points.
everyday.ex_us: They [[found that the complaint was valid]] on two of the three points.

note_fr: Usage britannique : un grief est « upheld », « partly upheld » ou « not upheld ». Usage américain : une allégation est « substantiated » ou « unsubstantiated ». Dans les deux cas, on se prononce allégation par allégation.

def: A complaint for which the investigation has not found enough evidence.

formal.ex: The third allegation was [[not upheld]] for lack of evidence.
formal.ex_us: The third allegation was [[unsubstantiated]] for lack of evidence.

everyday.uk: there isn't enough to go on
everyday.us: there isn't enough to go on
everyday.ex: It's not that we don't believe her; [[there isn't enough to go on]].

note_fr: Nuance capitale : « unsubstantiated » ou « not upheld » signifie que la preuve manque, pas que la personne a menti. « Unfounded » est plus tranché (dénué de fondement). « Inconclusive » = qui ne permet pas de conclure.

def: The letter telling the complainant or the respondent what the investigation concluded and what happens next.

formal.ex: The complainant will receive an [[outcome letter]] within seven days of the report being finalised.
formal.ex_us: The complainant will receive a [[closure letter]] within seven days of the report being finalized.

everyday.uk: to let someone know the outcome
everyday.us: to let someone know the outcome
everyday.ex: We owe it to her to [[let her know the outcome]], even if we can't share every detail.

collocations: to notify someone of the outcome
note_fr: « Outcome » = issue, résultat d'une procédure ; « result » conviendrait à un examen ou à un match. On ne communique pas à la personne plaignante le détail d'une éventuelle sanction : « appropriate action has been taken » est la formule habituelle.

fr: résoudre à l'amiable / de manière informelle
def: To settle a problem through discussion, without starting a formal procedure.

formal.ex: Wherever possible, concerns should be [[resolved informally]] in the first instance.

everyday.uk: to sort something out between themselves
everyday.us: to work something out between themselves
everyday.ex: My first question is whether they can [[sort it out between themselves]].
everyday.ex_us: My first question is whether they can [[work it out between themselves]].

informal.uk: to have a quiet word with
informal.us: to have a quiet word with
informal.ex: I'll [[have a quiet word with]] him before this goes any further.

note_fr: « To have a quiet word with someone » = prendre quelqu'un à part pour le recadrer en douceur, très britannique. « Amicably » existe (« to settle amicably ») mais s'emploie surtout pour les litiges. « To clear the air » = crever l'abcès.

def: To bring another person, such as a colleague or staff representative, to a meeting for support.

formal.ex: You are entitled to [[be accompanied]] by a colleague or a staff representative.

everyday.ex: You're welcome to [[bring someone along]] - a colleague or one of the staff reps.

note_fr: « To be assisted » signifie recevoir de l'aide, pas être accompagné. Au Royaume-Uni, le « right to be accompanied » est un droit légal lors des « grievance » et « disciplinary hearings », et la personne s'appelle « the companion ».

def: A situation in which a person's own interests or relationships could affect their impartiality.

formal.ex: Any person with an actual or potential [[conflict of interest]] must withdraw from the investigation.

everyday.uk: to be too close to it
everyday.us: to be too close to it
everyday.ex: I shouldn't run this one: I hired him, so I'm [[too close to it]].

collocations: to declare a conflict of interest
note_fr: Pluriel : « conflicts of interest » (« interest » reste au singulier). « To recuse oneself » est surtout américain ; au Royaume-Uni, on dira plutôt « to step aside » ou « to stand down ».

fr: représailles contre l'auteur d'une plainte (droit britannique)
def: Treating someone badly because they have complained of discrimination or helped someone else to do so.

formal.ex: Subjecting a witness to a detriment because she gave evidence in a colleague's grievance amounts to [[victimisation]].
formal.ex_us: Taking adverse action against a witness because she gave evidence in a co-worker's complaint amounts to [[retaliation]].

everyday.ex: She feels she's being [[punished for complaining]]: no bonus, no projects, nothing.

note_fr: Faux ami redoutable : en droit britannique, « victimisation » ne signifie pas « le fait d'être victime » mais les représailles subies après un « protected act » (plainte, témoignage). L'équivalent américain est « retaliation ». Orthographe américaine : victimization.

def: The obligation on one side to prove what it claims.

formal.ex: Once the employee has presented facts suggesting discrimination, the [[burden of proof]] shifts to the employer.

everyday.uk: it's up to someone to show
everyday.us: it's up to someone to show
everyday.ex: At that point [[it's up to us to show]] that the decision had nothing to do with her pregnancy.

collocations: the burden of proof lies with the employer
to bear the burden of proof
to discharge the burden of proof
note_fr: On dit que la charge « lies with » ou « rests on » une partie, et qu'elle « shifts » (se déplace). « Charge of proof » est un calque. En France comme au Royaume-Uni, la preuve est aménagée en faveur du salarié en matière de discrimination ; il ne s'agit pas d'un renversement complet.

fr: présenter des éléments de fait laissant supposer l'existence d'une discrimination

term.uk: to establish a prima facie case
term.us: to establish a prima facie case

def: To put forward enough facts for discrimination to be presumed unless the employer gives a convincing explanation.

formal.uk: to establish a prima facie case
formal.us: to establish a prima facie case
formal.ex: The claimant has [[established a prima facie case]] of discrimination, which it is for the employer to rebut.

everyday.uk: to show there is a case to answer
everyday.us: to show there is a case to answer
everyday.ex: The pay data alone is enough to [[show there's a case to answer]].

collocations: facts from which discrimination may be presumed
a prima facie case of discrimination
note_fr: « Prima facie » (à première vue) s'emploie tel quel en anglais juridique. Formule utile pour décrire le mécanisme français : « the employee presents facts from which discrimination may be presumed; the employer must then prove that its decision was based on objective factors ».

fr: éléments objectifs étrangers à toute discrimination
def: A legitimate reason, unrelated to any protected ground, that explains a difference in treatment.

formal.uk: objective factors unrelated to any discrimination
formal.us: objective factors unrelated to any discrimination
formal.ex: The employer must prove that its decision is justified by [[objective factors unrelated to any discrimination]].

everyday.uk: a good reason that stands up
everyday.us: a good reason that stands up
everyday.ex: Do we have [[a good reason that stands up]] for paying him more - experience, qualifications, anything on file?

collocations: a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim
note_fr: La formule britannique consacrée est « a proportionate means of achieving a legitimate aim » ; la formule américaine, « a legitimate, non-discriminatory reason ». « To stand up » = résister à l'examen (« it wouldn't stand up in court »).

fr: degré de preuve requis (enquête interne et procès civil)
def: The civil standard of proof: something is treated as established if it is more likely than not to have happened.

formal.us: by a preponderance of the evidence
formal.ex: The investigator finds, [[on the balance of probabilities]], that the remarks were made.
formal.ex_us: The investigator finds, [[by a preponderance of the evidence]], that the remarks were made.

everyday.ex: I don't need to be certain; I need to decide whether it's [[more likely than not]] that it happened.

note_fr: Ne confondez pas « burden of proof » (qui doit prouver) et « standard of proof » (jusqu'à quel point). L'enquête interne applique le critère civil, pas le « beyond reasonable doubt » pénal. Le droit français, lui, parle de l'intime conviction du juge : pas d'équivalent exact.

def: A change to the job, the workplace or working arrangements that enables a disabled person to work on an equal footing.

formal.ex: The employer is under a duty to make [[reasonable adjustments]] for disabled employees.
formal.ex_us: The employer has a duty to provide [[reasonable accommodations]] to employees with disabilities.

everyday.ex: What would we need to change to [[adapt the job]] - hours, equipment, where she sits?

note_fr: Piège majeur : « reasonable adjustments » au Royaume-Uni, « reasonable accommodation » aux États-Unis et dans les textes européens. « Accommodation » signifie aussi logement en anglais britannique. La limite s'appelle « undue hardship » (US) ou « disproportionate burden » (UE) ; en France, « mesures appropriées » sauf « charge disproportionnée ».

def: The French rule requiring employers above a certain size to employ a minimum proportion of disabled workers or pay a contribution.

formal.ex: Employers which do not meet the [[statutory disability employment obligation]] must pay an annual contribution.

everyday.ex: We're well short of the [[disability quota]], so we pay the contribution every year.

collocations: to fall short of the quota
to pay a contribution in lieu
note_fr: Notion sans équivalent : ni le Royaume-Uni ni les États-Unis n'imposent de quota général aux employeurs privés, et un interlocuteur américain peut y voir une pratique illicite chez lui. En France, l'obligation est de 6 % de l'effectif pour les employeurs d'au moins vingt salariés.

explain.written: The OETH (obligation d'emploi des travailleurs handicapés) is a statutory obligation under which French employers with twenty or more employees must ensure that disabled workers make up six per cent of their workforce, failing which they pay an annual financial contribution.
explain.spoken: In France there's a legal quota: once you have twenty staff, six per cent of them should be disabled workers. If you're below that, you pay a contribution every year instead.

def: A score out of 100 that French companies must calculate and publish each year to measure equality between women and men.

formal.ex: The Company's [[gender equality index]] for the previous year must be published on its website by 1 March.

everyday.ex: Our [[equality score]] dropped four points, mostly on pay rises after maternity leave.
everyday.ex_us: Our [[equality score]] dropped four points, mostly on raises after maternity leave.

note_fr: Notion française. L'index concerne les entreprises d'au moins cinquante salariés ; en dessous de 75 points, des mesures de correction s'imposent. Le dispositif est appelé à évoluer avec la transposition de la directive européenne sur la transparence des rémunérations : vérifiez l'état du droit avant d'en parler à un client.

explain.written: The index de l'égalité professionnelle is a score out of 100, based on a set of statutory indicators such as the gender pay gap and the distribution of pay rises and promotions, which French companies with fifty or more employees must calculate and publish each year; a score below 75 triggers an obligation to take corrective measures.
explain.spoken: Every French company with fifty or more staff has to publish a gender equality score out of 100 each year. If you score under 75, you have to put a corrective plan in place.

fr: à travail de valeur égale, salaire égal

term.uk: equal pay for work of equal value
term.us: equal pay for work of equal value

ipa.uk: /ˈiːkwəl peɪ fə wɜːk əv ˈiːkwəl ˈvæljuː/
ipa.us: /ˈiːkwəl peɪ fər wɜːrk əv ˈiːkwəl ˈvæljuː/

def: The rule that men and women must be paid the same not only for identical jobs but for different jobs that demand comparable skill, effort and responsibility.

formal.uk: equal pay for work of equal value
formal.us: equal pay for work of equal value
formal.ex: The principle of [[equal pay for work of equal value]] applies to all components of remuneration.

everyday.ex: On a [[like-for-like]] basis, the women in that grade are still paid three per cent less.

note_fr: « Like-for-like » = à poste comparable. Le salarié auquel on se compare s'appelle « the comparator ». Le droit fédéral américain est plus étroit : il vise l'« equal work », c'est-à-dire des postes en substance identiques.

def: Lawful measures to help an under-represented or disadvantaged group compete on equal terms, such as targeted training or outreach.

formal.ex: The mentoring scheme is a [[positive action]] measure aimed at women in engineering roles.
formal.ex_us: The mentoring program is an [[affirmative action]] measure aimed at women in engineering roles.

everyday.ex: The idea isn't to favour anyone; it's to [[level the playing field]].
everyday.ex_us: The idea isn't to favor anyone; it's to [[level the playing field]].

note_fr: Ne traduisez pas « discrimination positive » par « positive discrimination » sans précaution : au Royaume-Uni, la « positive action » est permise mais la « positive discrimination » (préférer un candidat en raison d'un critère protégé) est en principe illicite. Aux États-Unis, l'« affirmative action » fait l'objet d'un encadrement de plus en plus strict.

def: Attitudes or stereotypes that influence decisions about people without the decision-maker being aware of them.

formal.ex: All hiring managers are required to complete [[unconscious bias]] training.
formal.ex_us: All hiring managers are required to complete [[implicit bias]] training.

everyday.uk: to be biased without realising it
everyday.us: to be biased without realizing it
everyday.ex: We all tend to hire people like ourselves; you can [[be biased without realising it]].
everyday.ex_us: We all tend to hire people like ourselves; you can [[be biased without realizing it]].

note_fr: « Bias » se prononce /ˈbaɪəs/ et reste le plus souvent indénombrable ; l'adjectif est « biased » : « he is biased », jamais « he is bias ». « Prejudice » est plus fort et désigne un préjugé hostile.

def: The invisible barrier that stops women and minorities from reaching the most senior positions.

formal.uk: under-representation of women in senior positions
formal.us: under-representation of women in senior positions
formal.ex: The action plan addresses the [[under-representation of women in senior positions]].

everyday.ex: Plenty of women make it to manager; the [[glass ceiling]] is one level up.

note_fr: On « hits » le plafond de verre et on le « breaks » ou « shatters ». « Ceiling » : le c se prononce /s/. Variantes à reconnaître : « sticky floor » (plancher collant), « glass cliff » (falaise de verre).

fr: alerte protégée / signalement bénéficiant de la protection légale
def: A report of wrongdoing, or other step, that the law shields from reprisals.

formal.ex: An employee who makes a [[protected disclosure]] must not be subjected to any detriment for having done so.
formal.ex_us: An employee who engages in [[protected activity]] must not be subjected to any adverse action for having done so.

everyday.ex: As long as she acted in good faith, she's [[protected for reporting]] it.

note_fr: « Disclosure » = divulgation, révélation ; c'est le terme technique du droit britannique des lanceurs d'alerte. Aux États-Unis, « protected activity » est plus large et couvre aussi le fait de se plaindre d'une discrimination ou de témoigner. En France, on parle de « signalement » ou de « divulgation publique ».

fr: subir un préjudice / une mesure défavorable (à titre de représailles)
def: To be put at a disadvantage at work, for example by being refused a promotion, moved or disciplined.

formal.uk: to be subjected to a detriment
formal.us: to be subjected to an adverse employment action
formal.ex: A worker has the right not to [[be subjected to a detriment]] on the ground that he or she has made a protected disclosure.
formal.ex_us: An employee may not [[be subjected to an adverse employment action]] because he or she has engaged in protected activity.

everyday.ex: Nobody should [[lose out]] because they told the truth in an interview.

collocations: to be passed over for promotion
note_fr: « Detriment » est le mot du droit britannique, « adverse (employment) action » celui du droit américain. Le droit français énumère les mesures interdites : sanction, licenciement, mesure discriminatoire directe ou indirecte. « Prejudice » en anglais veut dire préjugé, pas préjudice.

fr: responsabilité de l'employeur du fait de ses salariés
def: The legal responsibility of an employer for wrongful acts committed by its employees in the course of their work.

formal.ex: The employer may incur [[vicarious liability]] for acts of harassment committed by its employees in the course of their employment.

everyday.uk: to be on the hook for
everyday.us: to be on the hook for
everyday.ex: If a manager harasses someone, it's the company that's [[on the hook for]] it.

note_fr: Au Royaume-Uni, l'employeur peut s'exonérer en prouvant qu'il a pris « all reasonable steps » pour prévenir les faits. En France, l'employeur répond du harcèlement au titre de son obligation de sécurité, sauf à justifier avoir pris toutes les mesures de prévention et réagi immédiatement.

fr: obligation de prévenir le harcèlement sexuel
def: The employer's legal obligation to act in advance so that sexual harassment does not occur, and not merely to react to complaints.

formal.uk: to take reasonable steps to prevent
formal.us: to take reasonable steps to prevent
formal.ex: An employer must [[take reasonable steps to prevent]] sexual harassment of its employees in the course of their employment.

everyday.uk: to get ahead of the problem
everyday.us: to get ahead of the problem
everyday.ex: Training once every five years isn't enough; we need to [[get ahead of the problem]].

note_fr: Le droit britannique impose désormais à l'employeur une obligation préventive (« to take reasonable steps »). En France, l'employeur doit prendre « toutes dispositions nécessaires » pour prévenir, faire cesser et sanctionner le harcèlement sexuel. « Preventative » et « preventive » sont tous deux corrects.

def: A narrow exception allowing an employer to require a particular characteristic, such as sex, when the nature of the job truly demands it.

formal.ex: A difference of treatment is permitted where it corresponds to a [[genuine occupational requirement]] and is proportionate.
formal.ex_us: A difference in treatment is permitted where it corresponds to a [[bona fide occupational qualification]].

everyday.ex: You can only specify a woman for the role if [[the job really requires it]], and that's very rare.

collocations: a genuine and determining occupational requirement
note_fr: Exception d'interprétation très stricte dans les trois systèmes : les préférences des clients ne suffisent jamais. Aux États-Unis, on dit couramment « a BFOQ » (en épelant). « Bona fide » = authentique, de bonne foi.
